title: Experiment Spec
description: One scenario plus a few sweeps that tell one story (RFC #21). The LLM designs this file; everything after it is deterministic. Structure only -- knob NAMES and GPU arithmetic are checked by scripts/validate_experiment.py against blis-vllm, blis-schemas and llm-d-router, which this schema cannot reach.

name.description: The experiment's identity; also the reports/<name>/ directory it writes.

description.description: Optional one-line summary of the question the whole experiment answers.

sweeps.description: The sweeps, in the order a reader should meet them. Each is one arm of the story.

scenario.description: Shared by EVERY sweep: one model, one hardware type, one workload, one GPU budget, one load ladder. Comparing two hardware types or two workloads takes separate experiments.

model.description: blis-catalog short-name, e.g. deepseek-v4.1-flash. A model runs iff the catalog carries it.

hardware.description: Scenario hardware key, e.g. h100. One per experiment.

workload.description: A catalog workload: a shape preset (chatbot, multidoc, ...) or a replay scenario (agentx-mvp). One per experiment.

gpus.description: The GPU budget EVERY run must use exactly. Combos that do not total this are dropped, so every comparison is like-for-like.

cluster.description: The cluster the scenario runs on. Today the one knob is the inter-node fabric, which prices cross-node traffic for a multi-node run. Omitted means ib-400g, so existing specs are byte-identical.

fabric.description: A blis-catalog networks/ class (ib-400g, roce-200g, ethernet-100gbe). A property of the cluster, not the GPU die -- an H100 fleet on RoCE must say so, or it is priced on InfiniBand. The validator checks the name against the sibling blis-catalog checkout.

checks.description: Service-level checks as registry figures with a bound (CFG-4). Validated against `blis metrics` now; applied from config search's M2 release. Until then a real run refuses them and `slo` applies.

max.description: Upper bound, in the metric's unit.

min.description: Lower bound, in the metric's unit.

objective.description: The figure the ranking optimises (CFG-4). Validated against `blis metrics` now; applied from config search's M2 release.

concurrency.description: The load ladder, set once here so every sweep is measured at the same levels. Closed-loop concurrency (sessions); for a replay these are session-tree lanes.

seed.description: The one seed every run of this experiment uses. Fixed so a re-run reproduces.

engine.description: Engine settings every run carries regardless of sweep (precision, context window). Single values, NOT lists -- these are not swept.

replay.description: Replay knobs when `workload` names a trace corpus: corpus_sha256, benchmark_duration, grace_period, max_context_length, category, thinking.

figureMetric.description: A metric registry identifier, as `blis metrics` prints it, e.g. ttft_p95_ms (DEV-8).

figureScope.description: cluster, pool or instance (design §8.7). The validator checks it against `blis metrics`.

figureAggregate.description: How a pool or instance scope combines, e.g. max for the worst instance. Not stated for the cluster scope.

slo.description: The caps a config must hold to count as servable. A config that misses any of them at a load is not servable at that load.

itl_p99.description: p99 inter-token latency cap, e.g. 20ms. The interactivity floor: 20ms == 50 tok/s/user.

throughput_per_gpu.description: Floor on output tok/s per accelerator, e.g. 500.

duration.description: A duration with an explicit unit: 20ms, 1.5s, 250us. A bare number is refused, because the unit is the whole meaning.

sweep.description: One arm of the experiment: a name, the question it answers, and knobs whose values are all LISTS. An omitted knob takes the vLLM default.

narrative.description: The hypothesis: what this sweep is expected to show and why. Carried into the report beside the measured result, so a reader sees the prediction next to the outcome.

num-instances.description: Replica counts for a COLOCATED sweep (a `blis run` flag, not an engine key). Mutually exclusive with the prefill/decode form.

parallel.description: Pool layout knobs for a colocated sweep: tp, pp, dp, pcp, dcp, enable_expert_parallel. blis-schemas names.

engine.description: Engine knobs, which are blis-vllm's engine-block keys (== vLLM's own config field names). `speculative` is the one nested block.

prefill-instances.description: Prefill replica counts for a DISAGGREGATED sweep. Requires decode-instances; BLIS refuses a prefill pool with no decode pool.

decode-instances.description: Decode replica counts for a disaggregated sweep. Requires prefill-instances.

prefill.description: The prefill pool's own layout and engine knobs.

decode.description: The decode pool's own layout and engine knobs.

allOf.description: A sweep is colocated or disaggregated, never both.
The two disaggregated instance counts come as a pair.

rolePool.description: One role's pool in a disaggregated sweep. BLIS requires the two pools to agree on block_size, KV cache format, dp and speculative config.

router.description: The llm-d router's own inputs. `endpoint_picker_config` names EndpointPickerConfig files BLIS runs unchanged; the override trees sweep fields INSIDE the named base file. Omitted means the llm-d default.

endpoint_picker_config.description: EndpointPickerConfig files, relative to routing/. A new routing policy is a new file, never an invented knob.

schedulingProfiles.description: profile -> pluginRef -> field -> list of values. Overrides fields the base file already has.

plugins.description: plugin name -> parameters -> field -> list of values. Field names are llm-d-router's own; it rejects unknown parameters.

engineKnobs.description: Engine knobs. Every value is a list, except the nested blocks (speculative, eplb, dbo, engram_config), whose own fields are lists.

speculative.description: Drafting. Needs BOTH method and num_spec_tokens -- acceptance comes from the registry, not a knob.

eplb.description: Expert-parallel load balancing; a nested block whose fields are lists.

dbo.description: Dual-batch overlap; a nested block whose fields are lists.

engram_config.description: Engram table placement; a nested block whose fields are lists.

knobLists.description: A mapping of knob name -> list of values to probe.

valueList.description: EVERY knob value is a list, even a single value: `tp: [8]`, not `tp: 8`. One rule, so a grid is always readable as a product.
